== Problem ==

Lucius is counting backward by <imath>7</imath>s. His first three numbers are <imath>100</imath>, <imath>93</imath>, and <imath>86</imath>. What is his <imath>10</imath>th number?

<imath>\textbf{(A)}\ 30 \qquad \textbf{(B)}\ 37 \qquad \textbf{(C)}\ 42 \qquad \textbf{(D)}\ 44 \qquad \textbf{(E)}\ 47</imath>

== Solution 1 ==
We plug <imath> a=100, d=-7</imath> and <imath>n=10</imath> into the formula <imath>a+d(n-1)</imath> for the <imath>n</imath>th term of an arithmetic sequence whose first term is <imath>a</imath> and common difference is <imath>d</imath> to get <imath>100-7(10-1) = \boxed{\text{(B)\ 37}}</imath>.

~Soupboy0

== Solution 2 ==

Since we want to find the <imath>9</imath>th number Lucius says after he says <imath>100</imath>, <imath>7</imath> is subtracted from his number <imath>9</imath> times, so our answer is <imath>100-(9 \cdot 7) = \boxed{\text{(B)\ 37}}</imath>

~Sigmacuber

== Solution 3 ==

Using [[brute force]] and counting backward by <imath>7</imath>s, we have <imath>100, 93, 86, 79, 72, 65, 58, 51, 44, \boxed{\text{(B)\ 37}}</imath>.

Note that this solution is not practical and very time-consuming.

~codegirl2013, athreyay

== Solution 4 ==

This can be thought of as an arithmetic sequence. Knowing that our first term is <imath>100</imath>, we have to add <imath>7</imath> to get to our  0th term, <imath>107</imath>. Our answer is then <imath>107 - 10 \cdot 7 = \boxed{\text{(B)\ 37}}</imath>.

~Kapurnicus, NYCnerd

== Solution 5 ==

Setting this as a function <imath>f (x)= 100- 7(x-1)</imath> where x is the xth number, we can plug in 10 for x. Quick arithmetic gives us the answer of <imath>\boxed{\text{(B)\ 37}}</imath>.

~themathkidwoohooooo
